title: Projective sheaf models from lisse residue cohomology on a weakly contractible affine
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi$, and residue field $k=R/(\varpi)$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $S$ be an affine weakly contractible scheme for its small pro-etale site [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], meaning that evaluation on $S$ sends every epimorphism of sheaves of sets to a surjection. For each open subscheme $U\subseteq S$, put $B_U=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(R/\varpi^n)_U$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit]. Let $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_S))$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Assume that $K$ is derived complete for its quotient tower, meaning that the quotient maps exhibit $K$ as a derived limit of $(K\otimes^L_{B_S}(R/\varpi^n)_S)_{n\geq1}$, with its canonical reduction transitions and all terms viewed in $D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_S))$ by restriction of scalars [def-weil-derived-limit, def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Assume also that its derived residue reduction $K_1=K\otimes^L_{B_S}k_S$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] has locally constant [def-weil-proetale-locally-constant-sheaf] constructible cohomology sheaves (locally constant with finite-dimensional $k$-module local models) with only finitely many nonzero degrees [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf, def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves], and has finite Tor amplitude locally: there are integers $a\leq b$ such that for every pro-etale $U\to S$ and every $k_U$-module sheaf $L$, the cohomology sheaves of $(K_1|_U)\otimes^L_{k_U}L$ vanish outside $[a,b]$ [def-weil-derived-tensor, def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Then there is a finite disjoint open covering $S=\coprod_i U_i$ [def-weil-open-immersion] such that, for each $i$, $K|_{U_i}$ is represented by a bounded complex of $B_{U_i}$-module sheaves whose terms are direct summands of finite sums $B_{U_i}^{\oplus r}$ (each summand has inclusion and retraction maps whose composite is its identity). The differentials are arbitrary $B_{U_i}$-linear sheaf maps; no constancy of their matrix entries over $R$ is asserted.

source.place: Tag 09C3 (lemma-local-structure-constructible-complex): weakly contractible affine, Noetherian coefficient ring, derived completeness, constructible locally constant residue cohomology and locally finite Tor dimension; finite disjoint open cover and completed finite projective module terms. Specialize Λ=R and I=(varpi); restriction of scalars between complete constant and completed coefficients is the equivalence of Tag 099I in algebraization.tex (lemma-restriction-derived-complete-equivalence). Tag 0990 (lemma-proetale-enough-w-contractible) supplies the covering context.

proof.text: The valuation ring $R$ is a principal ideal domain with nonzero uniformizer and finite residue field by [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr]; in particular it is Noetherian since each ideal has one generator. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-sheaf-reduction] to $R,(\varpi)$: $B_T$ is flat over the constant $R_T$ on any scheme $T$, and $B_T\otimes^L_{R_T}(R/\varpi^n)_T\simeq(R/\varpi^n)_T$. The constant sequence $0\to R_T\xrightarrow{\varpi^n}R_T\to(R/\varpi^n)_T\to0$ is exact (constant-sheaf exactness is clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-module-section-properties]). Tensoring it with the flat $B_T$ gives $0\to B_T\xrightarrow{\varpi^n}B_T\to(R/\varpi^n)_T\to0$. Thus $[B_T\xrightarrow{\varpi^n}B_T]$ in degrees $[-1,0]$ is a free resolution of the quotient, and is K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]. The quotient tower has epimorphic transitions, so [lem-weil-proetale-surjective-tower-derived-limit] identifies its ordinary limit $B_T$ with its derived limit, through the quotient maps; hence $B_T[0]$ and its finite sums and shifts are complete. We use [det-pe-derived-nakayama-first-reduction] for closure of complete complexes under cones and for detecting an isomorphism by its residue reduction. The statement of [det-prop-integral-criterion-constant-coefficients] explicitly identifies $B_T$ with $\mathcal O_{E,T}$ and identifies its quotient-tower completeness with [sk-def-pe-derived-completion], which is the completeness convention of the Nakayama node.

source.place: Tag 09C3, preliminary complete coefficients and derived Nakayama inputs; Tag 099I comparison supplied by the cited completed-coefficient lemma

proof.text: There are only finitely many nonzero sheaves $H^q(K_1)$. By their finite locally constant hypothesis, choose a common pro-etale covering, using finite base changes and compositions of coverings in [det-pe-topos-functoriality-site], trivializing them as constant finite-dimensional $k$-vector spaces. The covering definition [def-weil-pbc-proetale-covering], applied to the affine $S$, gives finitely many affine opens $V_j$ of covering members whose maps cover $S$; their restrictions retain the trivializations. Form $V=\coprod_jV_j$ using [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. The composite $V\to S$ is weakly etale by composition and source locality in [sk-lem-pe-weakly-etale-stability] (open immersions are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale], hence weakly etale by clause (1) of [det-pe-morphisms-etale-comparison]), and is a covering. The representables are sheaves by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-subcanonical], and $h_V\to h_S$ is an epimorphism: a section of $h_S$ locally lifts along this covering by its base changes. Weak contractibility of $S$ lifts $\mathrm{id}_S$ to a section $s:S\to V$; this is an actual scheme morphism by the definition $h_V(S)=\operatorname{Hom}_S(S,V)$. The inverse images $U_j=s^{-1}(V_j)$ form a finite clopen partition, since the coproduct components are clopen. The restrictions $U_j\to V_j$ pull back the chosen trivializations, so every $H^q(K_1)|_{U_j}$ is a constant finite-dimensional $k$-module sheaf. Discard empty pieces. This proves the needed partition directly from categorical weak contractibility; it does not assume the stronger ring-theoretic formulation of a w-contractible ring.

source.place: Tag 09C3, finite disjoint trivializing cover; expanded categorical proof of the covering step of Tag 098F, lemma-w-contractible-proetale-cover

proof.text: Fix a nonempty clopen piece $U$ of step 2. Restriction to $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$ is localization of $S_{\mathrm{proet}}$ by [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. Sheaf gluing for the disjoint open cover $S=U\amalg(S\setminus U)$ identifies sheaves, module sheaves, and their complexes with pairs on these two pieces: a sheaf on $U$ extends by zero on the complement, and sections on a disjoint union are products. Therefore a sheaf epimorphism on $U$ extends to one on $S$ by putting the terminal sheaf on the complement. Lifting its sections over $S$ proves weak contractibility on $U$. In particular evaluation on $U$ is exact on module sheaves: it preserves kernels sectionwise, and lifts sections of epimorphisms by weak contractibility. For any ring sheaf $C$ on $U$, $\operatorname{Hom}_C(C,F)=F(U)$ (a map is determined by the image of $1$); hence $C$ and every finite sum of it are projective objects. Restriction to a clopen factor is exact, commutes with all limits, quotient tensors and their Roos triangles under this product description, so $B_S|_U=B_U$ and $K|_U$ is complete with the same residue interval. The space $U$ is quasi-compact, being closed in the quasi-compact affine $S$.

source.place: Tag 09C3, restriction to the finite disjoint open cover; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0946, lemma-w-contractible, exact evaluation expanded from the defining lifting property

proof.text: On this fixed $U$ prove by induction on $b-a$ the stronger assertion: any complete $M$ whose residue cohomology sheaves are constant finite-dimensional $k$-vector spaces in $[a,b]$ and whose residue has Tor amplitude $[a,b]$ has a finite free $B_U$-complex representative with terms zero outside $[a,b]$. Apply [lem-sf-complete-residue-cohomology-bounds] to obtain $H^q(M)=0$ outside $[a,b]$. First note an explicit residue model: for each $q$ choose a basis of the constant $H^q(M_1)$. Exact evaluation on $U$ lifts these basis sections along the epimorphism from cycles of any representative of $M_1$ onto its cohomology. Sending each basis generator to its lifted cycle defines a chain map $\bigoplus_{q=a}^b k_U^{r_q}[-q]\to M_1$. It induces the selected basis isomorphisms on every cohomology sheaf, and is therefore a quasi-isomorphism by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Its source has zero differentials. Moreover [lem-pc-ring-derived-map-representative] applies to all the bounded complexes of finite free sheaves here, because their terms are projective by step 3. In particular $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(C)}(C^{r}[-q],N)=H^q(N)(U)^r$: chain maps are cycles and chain homotopies are boundaries, with exact evaluation commuting with these kernels and cokernels.

source.place: Tag 09C3, induction on the residue interval; Tag 09C2, lemma-describe-constructible-complexes, cohomological bounds; derived.tex Tag 064B, lemma-morphisms-from-projective-complex

proof.text: Put $r=r_b$ and $P=B_U^{\oplus r}$. The free quotient resolution $F=[B_U\xrightarrow{\varpi}B_U]$ in step 1 computes residue tensor even for an unbounded representative of $M$: choose a K-flat resolution $M^{\flat}\to M$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]; the maps $M^{\flat}\otimes F\to M^{\flat}\otimes k_U$ and $M^{\flat}\otimes F\to M\otimes F$ are quasi-isomorphisms by K-flatness of the two factors, the latter provided by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]. Consequently it yields the distinguished triangle $M\xrightarrow{\varpi}M\to M_1\to M[1]$. Its long exact sequence, supplied by [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact], gives a surjection $H^b(M)\to H^b(M_1)$ because $H^{b+1}(M)=0$. Exact evaluation on $U$ lifts the chosen $r$ basis sections of $H^b(M_1)$ to sections of $H^b(M)$, and then to cycles of a representative of $M$. These cycles define $f:P[-b]\to M$ inducing that basis on $H^b(M_1)$. By the Hom calculation of step 4 its reduction $f_1:k_U^r[-b]\to M_1$, under the zero-differential residue model chosen there, is exactly the inclusion of the degree-$b$ summand: a map from $k_U^r[-b]$ into that model has only its degree-$b$ component, determined by $H^b(f_1)$.

source.place: Tag 09C3, lifting the top-degree generators to a derived map; basis choice replaces the arbitrary top-degree surjection in the general-ring proof

proof.text: Complete $f$ to a triangle $P[-b]\to M\to L\xrightarrow{\delta}P[-b+1]$. The complex $L$ is complete by [det-pe-derived-nakayama-first-reduction]. Derived reduction is an exact triangulated functor by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], so $L_1$ is the cone of $f_1$. Under the residue decomposition in step 4 this cone is the direct sum of $\bigoplus_{q=a}^{b-1}k_U^{r_q}[-q]$ and the two-term identity complex on $k_U^r$, the latter contracted by the identity in the reverse direction. Thus $L_1\simeq\bigoplus_{q=a}^{b-1}k_U^{r_q}[-q]$. Its cohomology remains constant finite-dimensional; the displayed bounded free complex is K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site], and tensoring it with any $k$-module sheaf gives zero terms outside $[a,b-1]$, hence the required Tor amplitude. This supplies explicitly the amplitude decrease that the general source omits. When $a=b$, this residue is zero, so $L=0$ by the same derived Nakayama lemma; then $f$ is an isomorphism, and $P[-a]$ is the required one-term free model. If $r=0$ the same calculation has $P=0$ and still decreases the interval.

source.place: Tag 09C3, cone and induction; the sentence asserting decreased Tor amplitude, whose details are omitted there, is computed using the split residue complex

proof.text: If $b>a$, apply the induction hypothesis on this same $U$ to $L$, using the explicitly verified interval and constant residue sheaves of step 6. It gives a finite free complex $Q^\bullet$, supported in $[a,b-1]$, representing $L$. By [lem-pc-ring-derived-map-representative], the connecting morphism $\delta:L\to P[-b+1]$ is represented by a chain map $Q^\bullet\to P[-b+1]$. Only its component $Q^{b-1}\to P$ can be nonzero, and its chain-map equation is $\delta^{b-1}d_Q^{b-2}=0$. Form the shifted mapping cone $\operatorname{Cone}(\delta)[-1]$, using the cone and shift conventions in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. It has finite free terms $Q^q$ for $q<b$, term $P$ in degree $b$, and zero terms outside $[a,b]$; the last differential is the displayed sheaf map with its cone sign. The chain-map equation makes its composite with the preceding differential zero. Rotating the triangle of step 6 identifies this cone shifted by $-1$ with $M$, by the cone-triangle characterization of distinguished triangles. This establishes the induction step, including the actual sheaf differential needed to attach the top free term.

source.place: Tag 09C3, last paragraph: representing the connecting morphism and extending the complex by one term; derived.tex Tag 064B

proof.text: Apply the induction to $M=K|_U$ on each of the finitely many pieces of step 2. The hypotheses hold by step 3, and the residue cohomology vanishes outside the given $[a,b]$ by taking the tensor test sheaf to be $k_U$ itself. The resulting models even have finite free terms; each term is a direct summand of itself, with identity inclusion and retraction. The maps used to lift cycles and to represent $\delta$ are $B_U$-linear sheaf maps, so no step imposes constant matrix entries over $R$. If $S$ is empty use the empty partition and no models; if $K_1=0$ on a piece, derived Nakayama gives the zero model. This proves exactly the asserted finite disjoint open local models.

proof_origin.place: Tag 09C3, lemma-local-structure-constructible-complex, same top-degree cone induction, specialized to field residue and expanded via exact evaluation and split finite-free residue models; supporting Tags 09C2 and 099I.

lean.statement: theorem residue_lisse_projective_models (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : IsAffine S) (hweak : (Scheme.ProEt.topology S).IsWeaklyContractible.{u + 1} (Scheme.ProEt.mk (𝟙 S))) (K : DerivedCategory (integralTowerModules.{u, u} l E S)) (hcomplete : IsDerivedCompleteUnrestricted l E S K) (hresidue : intrinsicFiniteTorsionConstructible l E 1 (by omega) S ((scalarReductionDerivedExtension.{u, u} l E S 0).obj K)) (hlisse : ∀ q : ℤ, IsLocallyConstantProEtaleModuleSheaf S (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E 1) ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (proEtaleRingModules S (proEtaleConstantRing S (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E 1))) q).obj ((scalarReductionDerivedExtension.{u, u} l E S 0).obj K))) (hTor : HasFiniteProEtaleTorAmplitude S (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E 1) ((scalarReductionDerivedExtension.{u, u} l E S 0).obj K)) : ∃ (n : ℕ) (U : Fin n → S.Opens), (⨆ i, U i) = ⊤ ∧ Pairwise (fun i j ↦ Disjoint (U i) (U j)) ∧ ∀ i : Fin n, ∃ (P : CochainComplex (integralTowerModules.{u, u} l E (U i).toScheme) ℤ) (a b : ℤ), a ≤ b ∧ P.IsStrictlyGE a ∧ P.IsStrictlyLE b ∧ (∀ r : ℤ, ∃ (N : ℕ) (ι : P.X r ⟶ ∏ᶜ fun _ : Fin N ↦ SheafOfModules.unit (completedIntegralCoefficientSheafUnrestricted l E (U i).toScheme)) (ρ : (∏ᶜ fun _ : Fin N ↦ SheafOfModules.unit (completedIntegralCoefficientSheafUnrestricted l E (U i).toScheme)) ⟶ P.X r), ι ≫ ρ = 𝟙 _) ∧ Nonempty ((integralDerivedPullback l E (U i).ι).obj K ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj P)
